# Import necessary libraries
import frappe
from datetime import datetime, date

# Define the function to generate the report
def generate_inactive_items_report():
    # Define the filters for the report (e.g., inactive items and a specific time frame)
    filters = {
        "item_group": "All Item Groups",
        "is_sales_item": 1,
        "disabled": 1  # Filter for inactive items
    }

    # Get POS invoices for the specified time frame
    pos_invoices = frappe.get_list("Sales Invoice",
                                   filters=filters,
                                   fields=["name", "posting_date", "items"])

    # Initialize dictionaries to store last sale date and days since last sale for each item
    last_sale_dates = {}
    days_since_last_sale = {}

    # Process each POS invoice to find the last sale date for each item
    for invoice in pos_invoices:
        posting_date = datetime.strptime(invoice["posting_date"], "%Y-%m-%d").date()
        for item in invoice["items"]:
            item_code = item["item_code"]
            if item_code not in last_sale_dates or posting_date > last_sale_dates[item_code]:
                last_sale_dates[item_code] = posting_date

    # Calculate the days since last sale for each item
    today = date.today()
    for item_code, last_sale_date in last_sale_dates.items():
        days_since_last_sale[item_code] = (today - last_sale_date).days

    # Print the report header
    print("Inactive Items Report - Days Since Last Sale\n")
    print("{:<20} {:<20}".format("Item Code", "Days Since Last Sale"))
    print("="*45)

    # Print the report data
    for item_code, days in days_since_last_sale.items():
        print("{:<20} {:<20}".format(item_code, days))

# Call the function to generate the report
generate_inactive_items_report()
